blocks.content: Glaciers serve as the world's natural water towers, feeding perennial rivers and maintaining the global ecological equilibrium.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers store nearly 70% of the world's freshwater, acting as essential natural water towers for perennial river systems.
Major north Indian rivers such as the Ganga, Yamuna, Indus, and Brahmaputra originate from Himalayan glaciers.
Glaciers play a crucial role in regulating global climate by reflecting incoming solar radiation back into space via the albedo effect.
Glacial erosion and deposition form distinctive landforms including cirques, hanging valleys, moraines, drumlins, and eskers.
Accelerated glacial retreat driven by climate change increases the risks of sea-level rise and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs).

rows: Cover broad, continuous landmasses across thousands of square kilometers
Confined within steep mountain valleys and river channels
Flow outward in all directions from a central thick zone
Move downhill through existing valleys under the pull of gravity
Antarctic Ice Sheet and Greenland Ice Sheet
Siachen, Gangotri, Baltoro, and Hispar Glaciers

items: Siachen Glacier (76 km) in the Karakoram Range is the second-longest non-polar glacier in the world and holds strategic geopolitical importance.
The river Bhagirathi, a primary headstream of the Ganga, originates from Gaumukh at the snout of the Gangotri Glacier.
Frequently tested distinction: Cirques, Aretes, Horns, and Fiords are glacial erosional landforms, whereas Moraines, Eskers, and Drumlins are depositional landforms.
